title: Exact scalar restrictions, strict-system restriction and derived limit on one site
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l and W any scheme. With the independently sized completed and finite coefficient sheaves [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], there exists SiteData l E W [def-pur-completed-pushforward-models]. It includes exact derived scalar restrictions with their identity and composition normalizations, the quotient-generator-normalized finite ring identifications, the exact restriction of strict semilinear coefficient systems to completed-module towers, and a total right derived inverse limit with normalized projection maps.

source.place: Tags 0D6E and 0941, total derived functors and strict inverse limits; Zheng Construction 4.1 for coefficient systems

proof.text: Use the quotient of the ULift ring equivalence to identify the finite quotient rings. On quotient generators the equivalences commute with transition homomorphisms. Restrict each level of a semilinear system along the completed projection and inverse finite equivalence; restriction of the transition, transported through the ring equality, defines a strict tower.

source.place: Tags 0D6E and 0941, total derived functors and strict inverse limits; Zheng Construction 4.1 for coefficient systems

proof.text: Scalar restriction is exact on underlying abelian sheaves. Evaluation is exact and jointly reflects finite limits and colimits, hence the system restriction is exact. Exact localization gives its factors and the scalar identity/composition comparisons, normalized on all complexes.

source.place: Tags 0D6E and 0941, total derived functors and strict inverse limits; Zheng Construction 4.1 for coefficient systems

proof.text: Module sheaves and their strict towers are Grothendieck, so inverse limit has a K-injective total right derived functor. Apply its universal property to each ordinary projection. The right-derived factorization equation and cancellation of the exact evaluation factors give precisely the requested projection normalization.
